deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is a stratified space with two strata, an open stratum X* and a closed stratum Y. It comes with a tubular neighbourhood V = V_{Y,X} of Y, which retracts onto Y, and a 'punctured' neighbourhood V* = V*_{Y,X} = V \ Y. The maps are p: V* → V ≃ Y and i: V* → X*. This gives a diagram of fundamental groupoids Π1X* ← Π1V* → Π1V ≅ Π1Y, which is Grothendieck's diagram (18) of groupoids, or (10) of groups.

The previous page states the goal. One wants the category of sheaves F on X such that F|X* and F|Y are locally constant (sheaves constructible for the stratification). This category should be equivalent to the category of triples (E_{X*}, E_{Y,X}; φ):
- E_{X*} is a local system (étale covering) on Π1X*;
- E_{Y,X} is a local system on Π1V ≅ Π1Y;
- φ: p*(E_{Y,X}) → i*(E_{X*}) is a morphism of local systems on Π1V*.
The direction of φ is the cospecialisation map from stalks along Y to nearby generic stalks.

On this page, assume the three groupoids are connected (Y, X*, V* connected). Then the data become:
- a π1(X*)-set E_{X*};
- a π1(Y)-set E_{Y,X};
- a π1(V*)-equivariant map φ between them, where π1(V*) acts on both by restriction along π1(V*) → π1(Y) and π1(V*) → π1(X*).

The marginal NB, keyed to diagram (14), says connectedness is not really needed. With D = π1(V*_{Y,X}), φ can be read as a map (18 bis) E_{Y,X} → E_{X*} that is equivariant for the appropriate actions.

The page then introduces the 'typical case, important for algebraic geometry': X a topological surface and Y = {a} a point. Then V = D_a is an (infinitesimal) disk and V* = D*_a is a punctured disk. The next page reduces the group diagram to Z_{a,X} → π1(X\{a}), with Z_{a,X} → {1}. Here Z_{a,X} ≅ Z is the orientation module, i.e. the local monodromy (inertia) at a.

A constructible sheaf is then a π1(X*)-set E, a set F, and a map F → E. Since inertia acts trivially on F, this map lands in the inertia invariants E^{Z_a}. The next page adds that products of the model C* ⊂ C give the local models for normal crossing divisors.

This is the 1-categorical 'exit-path' (recollement) description of constructible sheaves of sets, written as representations of a diagram of fundamental groupoids. It serves Grothendieck's programme of 'dévissage' of stratified (tame) spaces. That programme aims at recovering the homotopy type, and here the constructible-sheaf category, from the diagram of fundamental groupoids of strata and tubular neighbourhoods.
errors: The previous page claims the reconstruction holds 'independently of local normal triviality'. Strictly, the equivalence needs tubular neighbourhoods V with V ≃ Y homotopically, and sections of F over V computed by stalks on Y. That is, a tame or conical (e.g. Whitney/Thom–Mather) local structure is still implicitly used. This is a gap rather than an error.
The margin NB is only partially legible. The precise equivariance statement in (18 bis) cannot be fully verified, but the reading 'φ as an equivariant map E_{Y,X} → E_{X*}' is consistent.

Minor point: in the surface example the target of φ is automatically contained in the inertia invariants E^{Z_a}. Grothendieck does not state this explicitly here, but it follows from his formulation.

ideas.what: Constructible sheaves on a 2-strata space are equivalent to triples (local system on the open stratum, local system on the closed stratum/tubular neighbourhood, morphism over the punctured neighbourhood)
ideas.modern_name: Exit-path category / recollement description of constructible sheaves (1-categorical); representations of the exit-path category
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson (unpublished, 1990s); Treumann (2009); Lurie (Higher Algebra, App. A); classical recollement in SGA4 / Beilinson–Bernstein–Deligne
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches the dévissage of stratified spaces via diagrams of fundamental groupoids of strata and tubular neighbourhoods, but not this explicit sheaf-theoretic equivalence as far as I know

ideas.what: Reformulation for connected strata as group-sets with an equivariant map along π1(V*) → π1(Y), π1(X*)
ideas.modern_name: Representations of a diagram of groups (van Kampen–type data)

ideas.what: Surface with a marked point: local data is the inertia Z_{a,X} (orientation module) → π1(X\{a}); local models for normal crossing divisors are products of C* ⊂ C
ideas.modern_name: Local monodromy / inertia at punctures; tame local models for normal crossings (cf. SGA1 XIII, SGA7, Deligne's Riemann–Hilbert)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. XIII (tame fundamental group, normal crossings); Esquisse d'un programme (orientation modules, discrete groups of surfaces)

missed.claim: An explicit 1-categorical exit-path description of constructible sheaves, as representations of the diagram of fundamental groupoids Π1X* ← Π1V* → Π1Y, is written out c. 1981. This predates MacPherson's exit-path idea and Treumann's/Lurie's published versions. It adds a priority detail rather than a new result.
missed.quote: Cette catégorie F est équivalente en effet à celle des systèmes (17) (E_{X*}, E_{Y,X}; φ) ... (18) φ : p*(E_{Y,X}) → i*(E_{X*})
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical credit: Grothendieck's 'dévissage' programme explicitly contained the exit-path classification of constructible sheaves, linked to his tame topology and anabelian concerns (orientation/inertia modules).

deep.surprise_reason: The content is mathematically standard today (exit-path/recollement description of constructible sheaves, local monodromy at punctures). Its explicit early form in Grothendieck's stratified-topos notes is a modest priority detail. The broad idea is already visible in Esquisse d'un programme.

The struck phrase after 'en considérant E_{X*} comme' appears to be 'un ensemble symétrique' or similar, replaced by 'un ensemble sur lequel π1(X*) opère'.

Margin: likely 'NB Dans le cas du diagramme (14), il n'est pas nécessaire de supposer ... connexes ... D = π1(V*_{Y,X}) ... on peut interpréter φ de (18) comme une application (18 bis) E_{Y,X} → E_{X*} ... π1(Y)- ... équivariante'. This reading is uncertain.
'disque (infinitésimal) autour de a' is correct; '(inf.)' abbreviates 'infinitésimal'.
